subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off TUI observer or mirror mode, and what transcript visibility boundary should it enforce across agents, sessions, channels, devices, and operators?
rationale: The code has plausible Gateway event primitives, but exposing cross-channel transcripts changes security expectations and likely adds public CLI/config surface, so automation should not choose the policy boundary.

options.title: Read-only observer first
options.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that displays only authorized activity for an explicit agent/session scope and defers bidirectional delivery mirroring.

options.title: Full bidirectional mirroring
options.body: Allow TUI and channel messages to appear across surfaces, but require explicit delivery, authorization, redaction, and upgrade policy before implementation.

options.title: No core mode
options.body: Keep logs, selected-session live tailing, or a future activity timeline as the supported monitoring path and avoid a core cross-channel TUI mirror feature.

recommendation.title: Read-only observer first
recommendation.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that displays only authorized activity for an explicit agent/session scope and defers bidirectional delivery mirroring.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily a product/security boundary, and this person has repeated recent TUI/session ownership signals plus project-direction context.
